request_contract_notes: Price APIs12452/12453/12454 require returnObj.data.isSucceed=true; renew/refund/unsubscribe12443/12440/20824 require returnObj.data.submitted=true in addition to statusCode200.

Database creation8899 requires collation and character classification for every documented character set except UTF8. Recovery provisioning12444 requires source identity and backup/time evidence according to the documented recovery flags.
Log purge10455 requires either a cutoff time or explicit file names; the documented default purge=1 compresses logs, while purge=0 removes them.

Resize APIs12442/12453 contain contradictory product-series requirements: prodId says prodPerformanceSpec is unnecessary, whereas azList says both are required. Presence-dependent resize validation is not supported by the condition schema. These constraints remain upstream-validated and are disclosed in help; no undocumented rule was invented.

Provisioning12444 marks subnetId and securityGroupId required in its table while describing them as optional during recycle-bin restoration. Required-column declarations are retained; no exposed recycle-bin discriminator is documented for a safe conditional override.

API12444 repeats backupStorageType twice in one request table with the same optional String contract. One CLI binding represents both rows; the second row has explanatory prose rather than a concrete example, so no value is invented.

gap_recheck.comparison: All six freshly retrieved document objects equal the retained captured-documentation.json entries.
gap_recheck.response_evidence: 19327/19328/19329 explicitly describe normal file-stream responses; 10436/18841/19317 put file-stream prose in the returnObj field. All six retain JSON response-envelope tables and empty HTTP status tables. No response Content-Type or Content-Disposition contract distinguishes a download from a business-error envelope.
request_discrepancies: 18841 declares /PG/v1/collector/slow-sql-export but its URL example uses /PG/v1/monitor/slow-sql-export.
19317 has no request body parameters but its body example contains unrelated database-extension installation fields.
gap_recheck.remaining_waiter_evidence: 8279 and 8887 expose instance and backup-name filters but no exact backup/task ID input; documented names do not establish unique task identity.

response_contract_notes: New order APIs 23992, 23995, 23967 publish no request or successful response examples. Preserve their JSON schemas without fabricated fixtures; statusCode 200 follows the existing accept-order-info platform contract. The billing-conversion schema calls returnObj a String while linking its newOrderId object table; the table supplies the display path, pending live interoperability verification.
request_validation_limitations: API 23967 constraints say month is required for prepaid instances but also defaults to one month when omitted, while the query table marks it optional. Keep month optional, declare the documented default 1 in shared help metadata, and show its prepaid-instance applicability in localized help. Omitted month remains absent on the wire so the upstream default applies; do not infer the instance billing type locally.
